candidates.title: Guardian foreclosure permanently stops the referee from accepting outputs of a tournament-settled state, and opens output execution (refunds, withdrawals) outside the outputs tree
candidates.component: Dave v3.0.0-alpha.7 DaveConsensus + cartesi-rollups-contracts 3.0.0-alpha.10 Application (deployed referee)
candidates.role: Referee model, as the deployed referee (AUDIT.md component table)
candidates.location: bugs/harness/work/dave/released/cartesi-rollups/contracts/src/DaveConsensus.sol: stageTournamentResult (l.167-196) and acceptStagedTournamentResult (l.246-287), both `notForeclosed(_APP_CONTRACT)`; the only write of `_outputsMerkleRoots` is l.272. dependencies/cartesi-rollups-contracts-3.0.0-alpha.10/src/dapp/Application.sol: foreclose (l.295, onlyGuardian, callable any time), issueRefund (l.186-215) and withdraw (l.257-281), which call _executeOutput on outputs built by REFUND_OUTPUT_BUILDER / WITHDRAWAL_OUTPUT_BUILDER without any outputs-tree proof.
candidates.description: Once the root tournament of epoch N reaches ROOT_WINNER, its winner's last leaf is the settled state (THREAT_MODEL A5: 'The settled state is the last leaf of the winning claim'). Recording its outputs Merkle root still needs two later permissionless calls (stage, then accept after the claim staging period). Both are gated by notForeclosed, and Application.foreclose() can be called by the guardian at any time, with no condition on the tournament or the staging window. After foreclosure, the outputs root of a state that the tournament settled (and that DaveConsensus may already have staged and verified as an rx-accepted yield) can never be recorded, so Application.validateOutput/executeOutput reject every output that only that state commits to, forever. The same holds at genesis for the outputs that the template commits to (see candidate 2). Foreclosure also enables issueRefund and withdraw. These execute outputs (vouchers built from an input or from an accounts-drive leaf) that no settled state's outputs tree commits to. A5 instead says 'An output is accepted only through a proof that authenticates a hash as a leaf of the full-height outputs tree'.
candidates.trigger: The guardian address named in WithdrawalConfig (any address chosen at deployment through DaveAppFactory.newDaveApp) calls Application.foreclose() after the epoch-N root tournament is finished with a winner, for example during the claim staging period, or before epoch 0 is ever accepted. Anyone then calls stageTournamentResult or acceptStagedTournamentResult, which revert with ApplicationForeclosed. executeOutput(output, proof) for an output at an index that only the epoch-N state commits to reverts with InvalidOutputsMerkleRoot.
candidates.reachability: Reachable on every deployment made with a non-zero guardian. No condition on the machine state is needed. The honest operator may have won the tournament and the settled state may be a perfectly valid rx-accepted yield.
candidates.rating_steps: 1. Out of scope? The list excludes defects that 'need the deployment to violate one of A1 to A8, unless ... an implementation of the referee model is what violates it (section 3)'. Here the deployed referee itself (DaveConsensus + Application) is what violates A5, so it is not excluded on that ground. If triage reads the guardian as a trusted deployment party outside the threat model (the model never mentions one), the finding is out of scope or Low. 2. Role: the deployed referee, 'Referee model, as the deployed referee' (AUDIT.md). Section 3: 'A defect in what it accepts or derives is rated as if a deployed referee had it.' 3. High/Medium cases: none fits. It is not an unreachable-state verifier issue, not a support component and not a cost issue. 4. Critical: it violates A5 at a reachable state. 'Conversely, the referee accepts every output that the settled state commits to, whenever its valid proof is presented. No party can make it stop accepting them.' The guardian is a party that can make the referee stop accepting the outputs of a tournament-settled state that was not yet accepted. It also violates 'An output is accepted only through a proof that authenticates a hash as a leaf of the full-height outputs tree' (refund and withdraw outputs). 5. n/a.
candidates.claimed_severity: Critical (literal A5). Alternative reading: Low or out of scope if the guardian is a trusted emergency role outside the model. The decisive fact is whether a guardian with these powers is a 'party' under A5.
candidates.threat_to_goal: Section 1 requires that no adversary can make the application 'accept an output that the settled state does not commit to', and A5 requires that the referee accept every output the settled state commits to. A guardian (or whoever holds its key) can freeze settlement after the honest claim has won. This permanently denies the outputs (vouchers, withdrawals) of the honest settled state, and replaces them with refund and withdrawal outputs computed outside the verified outputs tree from an older state (lastFinalizedMachineMerkleRoot).
candidates.evidence: Code reading only: _outputsMerkleRoots has a single writer (DaveConsensus.sol l.272) behind notForeclosed. foreclose() has no timing guard. issueRefund and withdraw call _executeOutput with no outputs-tree proof. Dave's own cartesi-rollups/contracts/AGENTS.md describes foreclosure as the intended 'emergency brake', so this is a design conflict with A5, not an accident.
candidates.test_idea: Forge test on the released Dave build. Deploy through DaveAppFactory with guardian G. Run epoch 0 with a single honest commitment until tournamentStanding()==ROOT_WINNER, then call stageTournamentResult with a valid MachineValidityProof whose tx-buffer word is root R committing to voucher V at index 0. vm.prank(G) app.foreclose(). Warp past the staging period. Assert that acceptStagedTournamentResult(0) succeeds and that app.validateOutput(V, proof) does not revert (required by A5). It currently reverts, with ApplicationForeclosed and InvalidOutputsMerkleRoot respectively, so the test exits 1.

candidates.title: Outputs committed by the valid template are refused until epoch 0 is accepted, and forever if it never is: DaveConsensus never records the template's outputs Merkle root
candidates.component: Dave v3.0.0-alpha.7 DaveConsensus (constructor, isOutputsMerkleRootValid) with cartesi-rollups-contracts Application.validateOutputHash
candidates.role: Referee model, as the deployed referee
candidates.location: bugs/harness/work/dave/released/cartesi-rollups/contracts/src/DaveConsensus.sol constructor (l.116-146): it receives initialMachineStateHash (the template hash) but takes no MachineValidityProof and writes no _outputsMerkleRoots entry. isOutputsMerkleRootValid (l.398-406) reads only that mapping. The contrast is Application._getLastFinalizedMachineMerkleRoot (Application.sol l.600-611), which treats the template as finalized when nothing has been accepted.
candidates.description: THREAT_MODEL defines the valid template as a state waiting at an rx-accepted manual yield whose 'tx buffer holds the outputs Merkle root of every output that the application accepted before it'. A5 says 'A valid template is such a state', meaning its outputs Merkle root is defined. The template is also 'The canonical hash that the epoch starts from, as settled on-chain' (A1). A template can commit to outputs, because it may have been 'changed only by running it and delivering inputs'. DaveConsensus never extracts or records that root. So from deployment until the first acceptStagedTournamentResult, every output the template commits to is rejected by validateOutput/executeOutput (InvalidOutputsMerkleRoot), even with a perfectly valid proof. If epoch 0 is never accepted (foreclosure, as in candidate 1, or a failed root), those outputs stay unexecutable forever. Meanwhile, withdrawals treat the same template as finalized. The two paths disagree on whether the template is settled.
candidates.trigger: Anyone presents a valid OutputValidityProof for an output that the template commits to (its tx-buffer root), before epoch 0's result is accepted. The guardian can make the refusal permanent by foreclosing before the first acceptance.
candidates.reachability: Reachable from any valid template whose outputs tree is non-empty (a template produced by running inputs offline, or a migrated application), immediately after DaveAppFactory.newDaveApp.
candidates.rating_steps: 1. Out of scope? It does not need a deployment to violate A1 to A8. The deployed referee is the implementation that falls short. The application is correctly designed. 2. Role: Referee model as deployed referee (AUDIT.md). 3. High/Medium: none of the listed cases. 4. Critical by literal reading: it violates A5 'Conversely, the referee accepts every output that the settled state commits to, whenever its valid proof is presented', at a reachable state, the genesis settled state. 5. If triage reads 'settled state' as only the result of an accepted tournament, the effect is a delay until epoch 0 is accepted, which violates no rule (Low). It still becomes permanent when combined with candidate 1.
candidates.claimed_severity: Critical (literal A5). Alternative: Low if the template does not count as a settled state for A5 or if a delay is acceptable. Medium if triage counts it as a manual contradiction without effect on the goal.
candidates.threat_to_goal: It refuses outputs that the settled genesis state commits to, which the referee 'must accept' (A5 conversely). Combined with foreclosure, or with an epoch 0 that is never accepted, the outputs are lost permanently.
candidates.evidence: Code reading. A grep shows the only writer of _outputsMerkleRoots is acceptStagedTournamentResult. The constructor emits EpochSealed(0, 0, ub, initialMachineStateHash, bytes32(0), tournament) with a zero outputs root.
candidates.test_idea: Build a valid template with the harness (configs/baremetal-template uses emit-output.bin: deliver one advance input so it emits an output and accepts, then store; or use valid-template, which emits a notice per input). Take its root hash as templateHash, deploy DaveAppFactory.newDaveApp, and build an OutputValidityProof for output 0 from the template's tx-buffer root (hash_tree frontier helpers). Assert that app.validateOutput(output0, proof) does not revert, as A5 requires for a settled accepted state. It reverts InvalidOutputsMerkleRoot, so the test exits 1.

candidates.title: Outputs up to the 2 MiB tx buffer can be committed by a correctly designed application but cannot be executed within the chain's per-transaction limits; nothing bounds output size the way A3 bounds inputs
candidates.component: cartesi-rollups-contracts 3.0.0-alpha.10 Application.executeOutput (with the emulator's tx-buffer size and machine-guest-tools libcmt emit functions)
candidates.role: Referee model, as the deployed referee (output acceptance); guest software (libcmt) for the producer side
candidates.location: Application.sol executeOutput/validateOutput (l.163-184, 328-351): the whole output is calldata, hashed, copied to memory by _executeOutput (bytes memory) and again for the call. AR_CMIO_TX_BUFFER_LOG2_SIZE = 0x15 (2 MiB) in the emulator and in solidity-step EmulatorConstants. libcmt src/rollup.c cmt_rollup_emit_voucher/emit_delegate_call_voucher accept any payload that fits the tx buffer. InputBox caps inputs at CanonicalMachine.INPUT_MAX_SIZE (64 KiB), but no counterpart exists for outputs.
candidates.description: A correctly designed application (THREAT_MODEL section 2: follows the rollup interface, yields accepted with the outputs root) may emit a voucher of up to about 2 MiB, and the settled state then commits to it. Executing it requires a transaction that carries the whole output as calldata, plus 63 siblings. Under the Ethereum per-transaction gas cap (EIP-7825, 2^24 gas) and the EIP-7623 calldata floor (40 gas per non-zero byte), any voucher above roughly 400 KiB of non-zero data cannot fit one transaction. That is before memory-expansion costs (quadratic, about 8.4M gas for 2 MiB) and the 128 KiB mempool transaction size limit. The deployed referee therefore can never accept such an output, although the settled state commits to it and its proof is valid. The model handles the input-side analogue explicitly (A3: 'It accepts no input so large that the honest proof of its delivery would exceed the chain's per-transaction limits'), but neither the emulator, the manual, libcmt nor the contracts bound or document output size.
candidates.trigger: An input makes a correctly designed application emit a large voucher (for example, an app that echoes or forwards payload-derived calldata, or batches many transfers into one multicall voucher). Anyone then tries to executeOutput it, and the transaction cannot be included.
candidates.reachability: Reachable: the tx buffer is guest-writable up to 2 MiB, and libcmt emits an output of any length that fits. A single 64 KiB input cannot directly carry that much, but application logic can aggregate state across inputs into one voucher.
candidates.rating_steps: 1. Out of scope? Possibly, under 'An application that is not correctly designed ... That exclusion covers only what such an application gets, which is its outputs'. But the application here meets the section-2 definition, which sets no size bound on outputs, so the exclusion does not obviously apply. 'An application that tries to exhaust the honest operator through the number of its outputs' is about count and honest-operator cost, not executability. 2. Role: the deployed referee for acceptance (Referee model). Guest software (libcmt) does not deviate from the documented interface. 3. High/Medium: none listed. 4. Critical by literal reading: A5 'Conversely, the referee accepts every output that the settled state commits to, whenever its valid proof is presented. No party can make it stop accepting them.' A valid proof cannot be presented within the chain's limits. The Critical list also has 'An honest proof or transaction that cannot fit the chain's per-transaction limits', but output execution is not on the honest operator's path ('Keeping outputs to prove them later is not on the honest operator's path'), so that entry probably does not apply. 5. Otherwise Low (a sizing gap the deployment should document, like A3).
candidates.claimed_severity: Medium (A5 vs per-transaction limits). Literal-A5 reading gives Critical. If output size is deemed the application's own responsibility, it is Low.
candidates.threat_to_goal: The application cannot obtain outputs its settled state commits to, so the 'conversely' half of A5 fails for large outputs. Funds held by the application that only such a voucher releases are stuck unless the guardian forecloses.
candidates.evidence: Constants read: AR_CMIO_TX_BUFFER_LOG2_SIZE=0x15 in the emulator Lua module and in both EmulatorConstants.sol. InputBox INPUT_MAX_SIZE check at InputBox.sol l.44. No output-length check in Application.sol or libcmt. Gas figures are arithmetic from EIP-7825/7623, not measured.
candidates.test_idea: On anvil started with --gas-limit 16777216 (EIP-7825 cap), build an outputs tree whose leaf is keccak of a 1 MiB voucher (Voucher selector + address + value + 1 MiB payload) and record its root through a settled epoch (or through a mock IOutputsMerkleRootValidator wired at the deployment block in a support test). Send executeOutput with the valid proof. Assert that the referee accepts it (required by A5). The transaction is rejected for exceeding the gas cap, so the test exits 1.

not_covered: Tournament internals (Tournament.sol matches, clocks, bisection, nested tournaments, elimination, bonds/refunds): only checked that ROOT_WINNER requires closed+no matches and that joinTournament authenticates the final state as the last leaf at full height.
CartesiStateTransition / regenerated solidity step and provideMerkleRootOfInput vs send_cmio_response input-root/length semantics (delivery path), not re-derived.
Did not run any on-chain experiment (no forge tests or anvil deployments). All three candidates come from code reading.

Withdrawal path details: LibAccountValidityProof and the withdrawal/refund output builders were not read in depth. Accounts-drive overlap with machine regions (for example tx buffer or shadow registers) is a deployment config that was not analysed.
machine-guest-tools beyond libcmt merkle.c/rollup.c emit and finish (rollup-http server, the rollup CLI's /tmp/merkle.dat persistence and load-failure behaviour, the ioctl driver) not audited.

The PRT player's output and proof collection in doc/recipes/prt.lua (support role) was not reviewed. Of the referee model, only game-output.lua validation and wait_for_outputs were reviewed (no defect found: fixed proof heights, index range, leaf hash and Lua type coercions all checked).
Sentry rotation edge cases and the DaveAppFactory/ApplicationFactory CREATE2 squatting (documented non-claim upstream) were not pursued.
Pre-deployment inputs to a predicted application address becoming epoch-0 inputs: noticed, not analysed for consequences.

Delegatecall vouchers able to rewrite Application storage (_executed bitmap, so outputs could be re-executed): not reported, because it needs the application to emit such a voucher (application design).
